chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked him about a man who gives his child to a Jewish, Christian, or Magian woman to breastfeed him in her house or to breastfeed him in his house.

He said: "A Jewish woman or a Christian woman may breastfeed him for you, and you should prevent her from drinking wine and from what is not halal, such as pork. And they must not take your child to their houses. And an adulteress must not breastfeed your child, for that is not permissible for you. And a Magian woman must not breastfeed your child unless you are compelled to resort to her."

key_terms.الزَّانِيَةُ: an adulteress, whose breastfeeding is not permitted
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: wine or intoxicating drink that must be prevented
key_terms.ظِئْرٍ: a wet nurse who suckles a child
key_terms.لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ: pork, cited as an example of what is not halal
key_terms.مَجُوسِيَّةٍ: a Magian woman, whose nursing is restricted here
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيَّةٍ: a Christian woman serving as wet nurse
key_terms.يَهُودِيَّةٍ: a Jewish woman serving as wet nurse

ai.seo_question: Can a Jewish, Christian, or Magian woman breastfeed a Muslim child according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out rulings concerning hiring a wet nurse from among non-Muslim women. It permits a Jewish or Christian wet nurse with restrictions regarding unlawful consumption and custody, while prohibiting an adulteress and generally prohibiting a Magian woman except in necessity.
